claim: Drosulfakinin (DSK) is a neuropeptide that is ortholog of Cholecystokinin (CCK) in mammals.
source: Drosulfakinin (DSK) is a neuropeptide, which is ortholog of Cholecystokinin (CCK) in mammals, and its two receptors (CCKLR-17D1 and CCKLR-17D3) have been identified in Drosophila (Chen and Ganetzky, 2012; Kubiak et al., 2002; Nichols et al., 1988; Staljanssens et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research establishing the orthology relationship between DSK and CCK.

claim: Two receptors for DSK (CCKLR-17D1 and CCKLR-17D3) have been identified in Drosophila.
source: Drosulfakinin (DSK) is a neuropeptide, which is ortholog of Cholecystokinin (CCK) in mammals, and its two receptors (CCKLR-17D1 and CCKLR-17D3) have been identified in Drosophila (Chen and Ganetzky, 2012; Kubiak et al., 2002; Nichols et al., 1988; Staljanssens et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research identifying these receptors.

claim: DSK peptide is involved in satiety/food ingestion.
source: Previous studies have revealed that DSK peptide is involved in multifarious regulatory functions including satiety/food ingestion (Nässel and Williams, 2014; Söderberg et al., 2012; Williams et al., 2014b), male courtship (Wu et al., 2019), and aggression (Agrawal et al., 2020; Williams et al., 2014a; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research on DSK function.

claim: DSK peptide is involved in male courtship.
source: Previous studies have revealed that DSK peptide is involved in multifarious regulatory functions including satiety/food ingestion (Nässel and Williams, 2014; Söderberg et al., 2012; Williams et al., 2014b), male courtship (Wu et al., 2019), and aggression (Agrawal et al., 2020; Williams et al., 2014a; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research on DSK function.

claim: DSK peptide is involved in aggression.
source: Previous studies have revealed that DSK peptide is involved in multifarious regulatory functions including satiety/food ingestion (Nässel and Williams, 2014; Söderberg et al., 2012; Williams et al., 2014b), male courtship (Wu et al., 2019), and aggression (Agrawal et al., 2020; Williams et al., 2014a; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research on DSK function.

claim: The 5'-UTR and coding region of Dsk were deleted by the CRISPR-Cas9 system to generate ∆Dsk mutant.
source: In brief, the 5'-UTR and coding region were deleted by the CRISPR-Cas9 system (Figure 1A), which was validated by PCR (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the method and validation by PCR shown in Figure 1.

claim: No anti-DSK signal was detected in ∆Dsk female brains.
source: No anti-DSK signal was detected in ∆Dsk female brains, whereas four pairs of neurons were detected in wide-type and ∆Dsk/+ female brains by immunostaining with anti-DSK antibody (Figure 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Four pairs of neurons were detected in wild-type and ∆Dsk/+ female brains by immunostaining with anti-DSK antibody.
source: No anti-DSK signal was detected in ∆Dsk female brains, whereas four pairs of neurons were detected in wide-type and ∆Dsk/+ female brains by immunostaining with anti-DSK antibody (Figure 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The anti-DSK antibody does not label the full set of DSK neurons.
source: No anti-DSK signal was detected in ∆Dsk female brains, whereas four pairs of neurons were detected in wide-type and ∆Dsk/+ female brains by immunostaining with anti-DSK antibody (Figure 1D), which does not label the full set of DSK neurons as previously found (Nichols and Lim, 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to previous research cited.

claim: Dsk null mutant displayed reduced copulation rate compared with wild-type virgin females.
source: Interestingly, Dsk null mutant displayed reduced copulation rate and prolonged latency to copulation compared with wild-type (Figure 1E) and ∆Dsk/+ virgin females (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Dsk null mutant displayed prolonged latency to copulation compared with wild-type virgin females.
source: Interestingly, Dsk null mutant displayed reduced copulation rate and prolonged latency to copulation compared with wild-type (Figure 1E) and ∆Dsk/+ virgin females (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Dsk null mutant displayed reduced copulation rate compared with ∆Dsk/+ virgin females.
source: Interestingly, Dsk null mutant displayed reduced copulation rate and prolonged latency to copulation compared with wild-type (Figure 1E) and ∆Dsk/+ virgin females (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Dsk null mutant displayed prolonged latency to copulation compared with ∆Dsk/+ virgin females.
source: Interestingly, Dsk null mutant displayed reduced copulation rate and prolonged latency to copulation compared with wild-type (Figure 1E) and ∆Dsk/+ virgin females (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: ∆Dsk virgin females displayed similarly low levels of ovipositor extrusion like wild-type and ∆Dsk/+ virgin females.
source: We asked whether the phenotype of decreased female receptivity in ∆Dsk flies is due to elevated rejection behaviors such as ovipositor extrusion, and found that ∆Dsk virgin females displayed similarly low levels of ovipositor extrusion like wild-type and ∆Dsk/+ virgin females (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Conditional overexpression of Dsk under the control of elav-GeneSwitch significantly increased copulation rate after feeding RU486 compared without feeding RU486.
source: Conditional overexpression of Dsk under the control of elav-GeneSwitch (elav-GS), a RU486-dependent pan-neuronal driver (Osterwalder et al., 2001), induced copulation more quickly than control females without RU486 feeding (Figure 1G and H, Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Conditional overexpression of Dsk under the control of elav-GeneSwitch shortened the latency to copulation after feeding RU486 compared without feeding RU486.
source: Conditional overexpression of Dsk under the control of elav-GeneSwitch (elav-GS), a RU486-dependent pan-neuronal driver (Osterwalder et al., 2001), induced copulation more quickly than control females without RU486 feeding (Figure 1G and H, Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Overexpression of Dsk in DSK neurons using DskGAL4 increased copulation rate compared with genetic control females.
source: In addition, overexpression of Dsk in DSK neurons using DskGAL4 also increased copulation rate and shortened latency to copulation compared with genetic control females (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Overexpression of Dsk in DSK neurons using DskGAL4 shortened latency to copulation compared with genetic control females.
source: In addition, overexpression of Dsk in DSK neurons using DskGAL4 also increased copulation rate and shortened latency to copulation compared with genetic control females (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Neuron-specific expression of Dsk using elavGAL4 could restore the decreased receptivity in ∆Dsk virgin females.
source: To address this question, we used the pan-neuronal driver elavGAL4 to drive UAS-Dsk expression in Dsk mutant background, and found that neuron-specific expression of Dsk could restore the decreased receptivity in ∆Dsk virgin females (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic rescue data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Activation of DSK neurons using dTrpA1 increased virgin female receptivity at 29°C relative to 21°C.
source: Activation of DSK neurons increased virgin female receptivity at 29°C relative to 21°C (Figure 2A)
evidence: The claim is supported by thermogenetic activation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Female receptivity was not changed between 29°C and 21°C in controls with either UAS-dTrpA1 alone or DskGAL4 alone.
source: whereas female receptivity was not changed between 29°C and 21°C in controls with either UAS-dTrpA1 alone or DskGAL4 alone (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by control data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Manipulation of DSK neurons did not affect ovipositor extrusion.
source: Meanwhile, we further analyzed whether activating DSK neurons would affect ovipositor extrusion in females with courting males and found that manipulation of DSK neurons did not affect ovipositor extrusion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Silencing DSK neurons by expressing tetanus toxin light chain (TNT) significantly reduced receptivity in virgin females.
source: We next tried to silence DSK neurons by using DskGAL4 to express tetanus toxin light chain (TNT), which blocks synaptic vesicle exocytosis (Sweeney et al., 1995), and found a significant reduction of receptivity in virgin females (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by neuronal silencing data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Activating or silencing DSK neurons did not significantly affect locomotion.
source: To test whether alteration of receptivity in females with DSK neurons activated or silenced is due to potential changes in general locomotion, we tested locomotor activity in individual females and found that the activating or silencing DSK neurons did not significantly affect locomotion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by locomotor activity data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Expressing Kir2.1 in DSK neurons decreased virgin female receptivity.
source: We further expressed an inwardly rectifier potassium channel (Kir2.1) that hyperpolarizes neurons and suppresses neural activity (Baines et al., 2001; Thum et al., 2006) in DSK neurons, and observed a decrease of virgin female receptivity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by neuronal silencing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Activation of DSK neurons did not alter female receptivity in young virgins.
source: We tested whether activation of DSK neurons could also promote female sexual receptivity in very young virgins or mated females, and found that activation of DSK neurons did not alter female receptivity in either young virgins or mated females (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Activation of DSK neurons did not alter female receptivity in mated females.
source: We tested whether activation of DSK neurons could also promote female sexual receptivity in very young virgins or mated females, and found that activation of DSK neurons did not alter female receptivity in either young virgins or mated females (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Four pairs of DSK neurons were specifically labeled in the brain by DskGAL4.
source: Analyses of the expression pattern of DskGAL4 revealed that four pairs of neurons were specifically labeled in the brain, which were classified into two types (two pairs of MP1 and two pairs of MP3) based on the location of cell bodies (Nichols and Lim, 1996; Figure 1—figure supplement 3D)
evidence: The claim is supported by expression pattern data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: DSK neurons were classified into two types (two pairs of MP1 and two pairs of MP3) based on the location of cell bodies.
source: Analyses of the expression pattern of DskGAL4 revealed that four pairs of neurons were specifically labeled in the brain, which were classified into two types (two pairs of MP1 and two pairs of MP3) based on the location of cell bodies (Nichols and Lim, 1996; Figure 1—figure supplement 3D)
evidence: The claim is supported by expression pattern data and citation to previous research.

claim: The two pairs of MP1 neurons were further classified into MP1a and MP1b based on the single-cell morphology.
source: and the two pairs of MP1 neurons were further classified into MP1a and MP1b based on the single-cell morphology of these neurons (Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Intersection of GluRIAGAL4 with DskFlp specifically labeled DSK-MP1 neurons.
source: Interestingly, we found that intersection of GluRIAGAL4, which targets glutamate receptor IA (GluRIA) cells, with DskFlp specifically labeled DSK-MP1 neurons (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by intersectional labeling data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Intersection of TβHGAL4 with DskFlp specifically labeled DSK-MP3 neurons.
source: while intersection of TβHGAL4, which targets octopaminergic neurons, with DskFlp specifically labeled DSK-MP3 neurons (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by intersectional labeling data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Activation of DSK-MP1 neurons significantly increased virgin female receptivity.
source: Activation of DSK-MP1 neurons significantly increased virgin female receptivity (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C)
evidence: The claim is supported by thermogenetic activation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Inactivation of DSK-MP1 neurons significantly reduced virgin female receptivity.
source: while inactivation of DSK-MP1 neurons significantly reduced virgin female receptivity (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by neuronal silencing data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Neither activation nor inactivation of DSK-MP3 neurons altered virgin female receptivity.
source: In contrast, neither activation nor inactivation of DSK-MP3 neurons altered virgin female receptivity (Figure 3E and F, Figure 3—figure supplement 2C-E).
evidence: The claim is supported by neuronal manipulation data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: DSK-MP1 neurons, rather than DSK-MP3 neurons, play an essential role in regulating female sexual behavior.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that DSK-MP1 neurons, rather than DSK-MP3 neurons, play an essential role in regulating female sexual behavior.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential effects of manipulating DSK-MP1 versus DSK-MP3 neurons.

claim: Mutation of CCKLR-17D3 reduced mating success rate in virgin females compared with wild-type and heterozygous control females.
source: Interestingly, mutation of CCKLR-17D3 reduced mating success rate in virgin females compared with wide-type and heterozygous control females (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: RNAi knockdown of CCKLR-17D3 under the control of the pan-neuronal elavGAL4 driver significantly reduced female receptivity.
source: Moreover, RNAi knockdown of CCKLR-17D3 under the control of the pan-neuronal elavGAL4 driver or CCKLR-17D3GAL4 also significantly reduced female receptivity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAi knockdown data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: RNAi knockdown of CCKLR-17D3 under the control of CCKLR-17D3GAL4 significantly reduced female receptivity.
source: Moreover, RNAi knockdown of CCKLR-17D3 under the control of the pan-neuronal elavGAL4 driver or CCKLR-17D3GAL4 also significantly reduced female receptivity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAi knockdown data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Conditional knockdown of CCKLR-17D3 using the elav-GS system significantly decreased female receptivity.
source: Conditional knockdown of CCKLR-17D3 using the elav-GS system to avert the potential developmental effect also significantly decreased female receptivity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C-E).
evidence: The claim is supported by conditional knockdown data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: No significant change of locomotor activity was detected in CCKLR-17D3 mutant or knockdown females.
source: In addition, no significant change of locomotor activity was detected in CCKLR-17D3 mutant or knockdown females (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by locomotor activity data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The reduced female receptivity of CCKLR-17D3 mutant females could be rescued by expression of UAS-CCKLR-17D3 driven by elav-GS.
source: Furthermore, the reduced female receptivity of CCKLR-17D3 mutant females could be rescued by expression of UAS-CCKLR-17D3 driven by elav-GS (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic rescue data shown in Figure 4E-G.

claim: DSK acts through CCKLR-17D3 but not CCKLR-17D1 to promote female sexual receptivity.
source: These results demonstrate that DSK acts through CCKLR-17D3 but not CCKLR-17D1 to promote female sexual receptivity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential effects of manipulating CCKLR-17D3 versus CCKLR-17D1.

claim: Activating CCKLR-17D3GAL4 neurons using dTrpA1 significantly increased mating success rate in virgin females at 29°C than 21°C.
source: We activated CCKLR-17D3GAL4 neurons using dTrpA1 and observed significantly increased mating success rate in virgin females at 29°C than 21°C (Figure 4H)
evidence: The claim is supported by thermogenetic activation data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Female receptivity was not changed between 29°C and 21°C in control females for CCKLR-17D3GAL4 activation.
source: whereas female receptivity was not changed between 29°C and 21°C in control females (Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by control data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Inactivating CCKLR-17D3GAL4 neurons by expressing TNT decreased female receptivity.
source: Moreover, we also inactivated CCKLR-17D3GAL4 neurons by expressing TNT and found that female receptivity was decreased after inactivating these neurons (Figure 4J).
evidence: The claim is supported by neuronal silencing data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: CCKLR-17D3GAL4 neurons positively regulate virgin female receptivity.
source: Thus, CCKLR-17D3GAL4 neurons positively regulate virgin female receptivity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the effects of activating and inactivating CCKLR-17D3GAL4 neurons.

claim: Intersection between CCKLR-17D3GAL4 and dsxLexA only labeled projections from peripheral sensory neurons that innervate the SOG region.
source: However, intersection between CCKLR-17D3GAL4 and dsxLexA only labeled projections from peripheral sensory neurons that innervate the SOG region (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by intersectional labeling data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Either overexpressing or knocking down CCKLR-17D3 in all dsx neurons did not alter virgin female receptivity.
source: Furthermore, either overexpressing or knocking down CCKLR-17D3 in all dsx neurons did not alter virgin female receptivity (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic manipulation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C,D.

claim: CCKLR-17D3 did not function in dsx neurons to regulate female sexual behavior.
source: These results indicate that CCKLR-17D3 did not function in dsx neurons to regulate female sexual behavior.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of effect when manipulating CCKLR-17D3 in dsx neurons.

claim: Loss of CCKLR-17D3 function could block the increased levels of female receptivity caused by activating DSK neurons.
source: We found that loss of CCKLR-17D3 function could block the increased levels of female receptivity caused by activating DSK neurons (Figure 4K–M).
evidence: The claim is supported by epistasis data shown in Figure 4K-M.

claim: DSK released from DSK-MP1 neurons acts on its receptor CCKLR-17D3 to promote female sexual receptivity.
source: Together these results demonstrate that DSK released from DSK-MP1 neurons acts on its receptor CCKLR-17D3 to promote female sexual receptivity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of DSK and CCKLR-17D3 manipulations.

claim: R71G01-GAL4 drives the expression of P1 neurons that interact with DSK neurons to regulate male courtship.
source: In males, R71G01-GAL4 drives the expression of P1 neurons that interact with DSK neurons to regulate male courtship (Wu et al., 2019) and aggression (Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: R71G01-GAL4 drives the expression of P1 neurons that interact with DSK neurons to regulate aggression.
source: In males, R71G01-GAL4 drives the expression of P1 neurons that interact with DSK neurons to regulate male courtship (Wu et al., 2019) and aggression (Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The intersection of R71G01-LexA with dsxGAL4 specifically labels and manipulates pC1 neurons.
source: Previous studies employed the intersection of R71G01-LexA with dsxGAL4 to specifically label and manipulate pC1 neurons, which integrate male courtship and pheromone cues to promote virgin female receptivity (Wang et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: pC1 neurons integrate male courtship and pheromone cues to promote virgin female receptivity.
source: Previous studies employed the intersection of R71G01-LexA with dsxGAL4 to specifically label and manipulate pC1 neurons, which integrate male courtship and pheromone cues to promote virgin female receptivity (Wang et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons promoted female receptivity.
source: We found that activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons consisting of pC1 and a few other neurons promoted female receptivity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by thermogenetic activation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Significant reconstituted GFP signals were detected between R71G01-LexA and DskGAL4 labeled neurons using GRASP.
source: Interestingly, we detected significant reconstituted GFP signals between R71G01-LexA and DskGAL4 labeled neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by GRASP data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: R71G01-GAL4 downstream trans-Tango signals were observed in DSK neurons.
source: Interestingly, R71G01-GAL4 downstream trans-Tango signals were observed in DSK neurons by co-staining the trans-Tango flies with the anti-DSK antibody (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by trans-Tango data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Axons of R71G01-GAL4 neurons partly overlapped with dendrites of DSK neurons.
source: Moreover, we registrated R71G01-GAL4 neurons and DSK neurons, and found that axons of R71G01-GAL4 neurons partly overlapped with dendrites of DSK neurons (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical registration data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Increased levels of female receptivity caused by activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons were suppressed by the mutation in Dsk.
source: We activated R71G01-GAL4 neurons by dTrpA1 in the Dsk mutant background, and found that increased levels of female receptivity caused by activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons were suppressed by the mutation in Dsk (Figure 5D–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by epistasis data shown in Figure 5D-G.

claim: DSK neurons are the functional targets of R71G01-GAL4 neurons in controlling female sexual behavior.
source: Taken together, these results further demonstrate that DSK neurons are the functional targets of R71G01-GAL4 neurons in controlling female sexual behavior.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined anatomical and functional data.

claim: Axons of pC1 neurons overlapped with dendrites of DSK neurons.
source: We registrated pC1 neurons labeled by two independent pC1 splitGAL4 (pC1-ss1 and pC1-ss2) with DSK neurons, and found that axons of pC1 neurons overlapped with dendrites of DSK neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical registration data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: pC1 neurons have intense synaptic input on DSK-MP1 neurons, especially the single pair of DSK-MP1b neurons.
source: Furthermore, we utilized the recently generated full adult female brain (FAFB) electron microscopic (EM) image set (Scheffer et al., 2020), and found that pC1 neurons have intense synaptic input on DSK-MP1 neurons, especially the single pair of DSK-MP1b neurons, and few input on DSK-MP3 neurons (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by EM connectomics data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: pC1 neurons have few synaptic input on DSK-MP3 neurons.
source: Furthermore, we utilized the recently generated full adult female brain (FAFB) electron microscopic (EM) image set (Scheffer et al., 2020), and found that pC1 neurons have intense synaptic input on DSK-MP1 neurons, especially the single pair of DSK-MP1b neurons, and few input on DSK-MP3 neurons (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by EM connectomics data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: DSK neurons are direct targets of R71G01-GAL4 labeled pC1 neurons.
source: These results indicate that DSK neurons are direct targets of R71G01-GAL4 labeled pC1 neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined anatomical and EM data.

claim: ATP/P2X2 activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons induced strong electrical responses from DSK-MP1 neurons in female brains.
source: In perforate patch recordings, ATP/P2X2 activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons induced strong electrical responses from DSK-MP1 neurons and relatively weaker responses from DSK-MP3 neurons in female brains (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: ATP/P2X2 activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons induced relatively weaker electrical responses from DSK-MP3 neurons in female brains.
source: In perforate patch recordings, ATP/P2X2 activation of R71G01-GAL4 neurons induced strong electrical responses from DSK-MP1 neurons and relatively weaker responses from DSK-MP3 neurons in female brains (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Dsk-expressing DSK-MP1 neurons receive input from sex-promoting pC1 neurons.
source: Thus, these results together with the above EM data unambiguously demonstrate that Dsk-expressing DSK-MP1 neurons receive input from sex-promoting pC1 neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined electrophysiological and EM data.

claim: Knocking down Dsk expression pan-neuronally significantly decreased DSK immunoreactivity.
source: To further confirm the decreased receptivity phenotype in ∆Dsk females, we knocked down the expression of Dsk using RNA interference (RNAi) under the control of a pan-neuronal elavGAL4 driver, which significantly decreased DSK immunoreactivity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B.

claim: Knocking down Dsk expression pan-neuronally significantly reduced female receptivity.
source: We found that knocking down Dsk expression pan-neuronally significantly reduced female receptivity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Reduced female receptivity was observed in females with Dsk knockdown using DskGAL4.
source: Furthermore, we also observed reduced female receptivity in females with Dsk knockdown using a knock-in DskGAL4 generated previously (Wu et al., 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 3D-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3F.

claim: DskGAL4 only labeled four pairs of neurons in the brain and no expression in the glia or gut.
source: This DskGAL4 only labeled four pairs of neurons in the brain and no expression in the glia or gut (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D-E).
evidence: The claim is supported by expression pattern data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D-E.

claim: DskGAL4 did not label insulin-producing cells (IPCs) in the PI region.
source: It should be mentioned that this DskGAL4 did not label insulin-producing cells (IPCs) in the PI region as previously found (Nichols and Lim, 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to previous research cited.

claim: Restricting the expression of DskRNAi in IPCs using Dilp2-GAL4 did not affect virgin female receptivity.
source: Thus, to investigate whether DSK peptide released from IPCs is involved in female sexual behavior, we knocked down the expression of Dsk only in these IPCs by using Dilp2-GAL4 and found that restricting the expression of DskRNAi in IPCs did not affect virgin female receptivity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3G.

claim: No significant change of locomotor activity was detected in females with Dsk mutant.
source: No significant change of locomotor activity was detected in females with Dsk mutant or knockdown (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by locomotor activity data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: No significant change of locomotor activity was detected in females with Dsk knockdown.
source: No significant change of locomotor activity was detected in females with Dsk mutant or knockdown (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by locomotor activity data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Wild-type males paired with ∆Dsk females showed similarly high levels of courtship as control females.
source: To investigate whether reduced copulation rate in ∆Dsk females is due to potential abatement of female sexual appeal, we examined courtship levels in wild-type males paired with ∆Dsk or control females and observed similarly high levels of courtship in all cases (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by courtship data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The decreased receptivity in ∆Dsk females is not due to any change in male courtship efficiency, but rather a decline of willingness for copulation in these females.
source: Thus, the decreased receptivity in ∆Dsk females is not due to any change in male courtship efficiency, but rather a decline of willingness for copulation in these females.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that male courtship levels were unchanged.

claim: Manipulation of Dsk did not enhance egg laying in virgin females.
source: To address this, we examined the number of eggs laid by virgin females with Dsk mutant or knockdown, and found that manipulation of Dsk did not enhance egg laying in these virgin females (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by egg laying data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: TRIC signals were only observed in the two pairs of neurons in the middle area of female brains labeled by DskGAL4.
source: As mentioned above, four pairs of neurons were labeled by DskGAL4 driving the expression of UAS-mCD8::GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D). However, we only observed TRIC signals in the two pairs of neurons in the middle area of female brains (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by TRIC data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6B,C.

claim: Quantification of TRIC signals showed no significant difference in virgin and mated females.
source: Quantification of these TRIC signals showed no significant difference in virgin and mated females (Figure 1—figure supplement 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by TRIC quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6D.

claim: DSK neurons do not respond to mating status.
source: These results further indicate that DSK neurons do not respond to mating status.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of difference in TRIC signals between virgin and mated females.

claim: Mutation of CCKLR-17D1 did not affect virgin female receptivity.
source: We first examined virgin female receptivity in either CCKLR-17D1 mutant female, which was generated previously (Wu et al., 2020), or CCKLR-17D1 RNAi knockdown female, and did not observe any effect on female receptivity (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.
